payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Compared with SOURCE, is her jacket fully closed in EDITED?
node.criteria: Compare the same jacket on the woman in SOURCE and EDITED. Assess whether the front panels have moved together toward closure; full achievement requires the panels to meet so no visible opening remains along the closure.
node.binding: Compare the jacket on the woman in SOURCE with the jacket on the woman in EDITED; judge progress toward the requested endpoint of a fully closed jacket, distinguishing no visible progress, concrete partial closure, and full closure.
node.endpoint: Her jacket is fully closed, with no visible opening along the closure.
node.necessity: This is the requested change and its complete endpoint.
node.zero_when: The same jacket shows no visible movement of its front panels toward one another compared with SOURCE; it remains equally open or more open.
node.half_when: The front panels show concrete movement toward one another compared with SOURCE, but a visible opening remains along the closure; this is incomplete progress, not full closure.
node.full_when: The front panels meet and no visible opening remains along the jacket closure.

node_traces.evidence: The jacket is open in SOURCE, with a visible gap between its front panels. In EDITED, the jacket remains visibly open and the panels do not appear to have moved together toward closure; no concrete progress toward the requested fully closed state is evident.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s binding currently collapses the rubric’s three outcomes into a binary “equally open or more open” test, so it can label concrete partial closure as no progress. Preserve the explicit zero/partial/full distinctions: compare the same jacket’s front panels across images, count visible movement toward one another as partial progress even if an opening remains, and reserve full fulfillment for panels meeting with no visible opening. In these images the woman turns and the jacket’s pose/drape changes, so avoid treating pose or apparent panel displacement alone as closure; assess the closure line and use unresolved when the comparison is obscured or insufficient. The trace is a valid visual judgment with no transport, schema, or dependency failure; its stated evidence supports no progress, but the reference-label disagreement is not by itself proof that progress occurred. Recheck whether the changed viewpoint/pose hides a genuine panel movement before assigning zero, and calibrate confidence to that visibility."}
